payload.text:
Don't merge this yet: `canEdit` is broken. All the tests pass, but they miss the bug. I only read the code and ran the tests; nothing was changed.

**Has to be fixed: `canEdit` in `src/guard.js`**
```js
return share.mask & WRITE === WRITE && !share.locked;
```
In JavaScript, `===` is evaluated before `&`, so this is really `share.mask & (WRITE === WRITE)`. That works out to `mask & 1`, which only checks the READ bit. I tried it:
- A view-only share (`mask: READ`) on an unlocked doc gets **true**, so viewers can edit.
- A share with COMMENT and WRITE but no READ (`mask: 6`) gets **0**, so it can't edit.

The test doesn't catch this because the editor share it uses has READ too. Two possible fixes: use `hasRight(share.mask, WRITE)` like `canComment` does, or add brackets: `(share.mask & WRITE) === WRITE`. Either way, add a test checking that a READ-only share can't edit.

**Worth looking at**
- **`transferOwnership` doesn't check anything.** It never confirms that `fromUser` is the current owner or has ADMIN. If the caller doesn't check, anyone can hand a doc to anyone. Also, if `fromUser` has no share, it quietly creates one with no rights (`undefined & ~ADMIN` → 0).
- **Toggle tests only cover one direction.** `toggleRight` uses XOR, which matches the README. But there's no test for a switch turning a right *off*, and nothing stops the owner from turning off their own ADMIN or READ in the dialog.
- **The changelog for 3.2.0 is incomplete.** It only lists editing and locking. The share-dialog switches and ownership transfer, both new in this branch, aren't mentioned.

Everything else looks right: `canComment`, locking, and transfer keeping the previous owner's rights apart from ADMIN all match what the README says.
